answer.because: On head, parsing `--x 2 --x 1` gives `x = 3` where base gives `[2, 1]`: setKey's `value === increment()` test treats the ordinary number 1 as a count increment on a key that isn't a count, so the duplicate-array handling never runs (the finding's second case, `--x 1` with array:['x'], still gives [1] on head, so the check only asserts the repeated-option case and a passing count case).

base.output_tail:
PASS --x 2 --x 1 (repeated numeric option) [2,1]
PASS --x 1 with array:['x'] [1]
PASS count still works: -vvv 3

head.output_tail:
FAIL --x 2 --x 1 (repeated numeric option) got 3 expected [2,1]
PASS --x 1 with array:['x'] [1]
PASS count still works: -vvv 3

why: On head, parsing `--x 2 --x 1` gives `x = 3` where base gives `[2, 1]`: setKey's `value === increment()` test treats the ordinary number 1 as a count increment on a key that isn't a count, so the duplicate-array handling never runs (the finding's second case, `--x 1` with array:['x'], still gives [1] on head, so the check only asserts the repeated-option case and a passing count case).
